title: Getting Zoning Information Before Buying Land or Building 2026
desc: How to get zoning information before buying land or building in 2026: what you can see, which authority to ask, published plans and boundary-marker records.
summary: What zoning information the public may access, which authority to ask, and what to read in the plan before paying for land or designing a house.
body: p

Buying a plot that falls within planned road space, or finishing a design only to learn that the building line sets back several metres, is not unusual. Under Article 55 of the Law on Urban and Rural Planning No. 47/2024/QH15 (as amended by Law 144/2025/QH15, effective 1 January 2026), the public has the right to be provided with zoning information. This article explains how.
h2
1. Why check the zoning plan first?
ul

A condition for a construction permit is that the work conforms to the urban and rural zoning plan, the specific urban design or the architectural management regulations (Point b, Clause 1, Article 44 of the Construction Law 2025).
A detached house is exempt from a permit only if it is not located in the planned areas listed in Point g, Clause 2, Article 43 – see Which Detached Houses Are Exempt from a Construction Permit?
h2
2. What information can the public access?
p
Under Clause 1, Article 55, agencies, organisations and individuals may access:
ul
Urban and rural zoning plans that have been approved and announced;
Issued zoning management regulations and plans for implementing general plans;
Information on administrative procedures and legal documents on planning.
h2
3. Which authority to ask?
p
Under Clause 2, Article 55 (as amended by Clause 35, Article 1 of Law 144/2025/QH15), the bodies responsible for providing approved zoning information on request are:
ul
The specialised urban and rural planning agency under the provincial People's Committee;
The specialised agency with planning management functions under the commune-level People's Committee (commune or ward);
The agency or organisation assigned to manage a functional zone (economic zone, tourism zone, etc.).
p

The providing agency is responsible for the accuracy of the documents and data supplied. The method of providing information on request follows the regulations of the Minister of Construction (Clause 3, Article 55 as amended). In practice, homeowners usually start at the land-and-construction desk of the ward or commune People's Committee where the land is located.
h2
4. Looking up published plans yourself
p

Under Article 50, within 15 days of approval a plan must be publicly announced, including the approval decision, drawings, explanatory report and zoning management regulations. The plan is announced at the head office and posted regularly on the website of the agency that organised the planning and on the national planning information system. Digitised planning records are announced by the provincial People's Committee on the Ministry of Construction's planning portal (Point dd, Clause 1, Article 24 of Decree 178/2025/ND-CP).
h2
5. Asking about boundary markers and red lines
p

For detailed plans, the State sets markers for the red line, building line and construction elevation and the boundaries of construction-ban areas (Clause 1, Article 52). The specialised planning agencies under the provincial and commune People's Committees keep the marker-setting records and provide marker information on request (Clause 4, Article 52, as amended by Clause 33, Article 1 of Law 144/2025/QH15). The information is answered in writing or provided as a copy of the approved marker-setting drawings (Article 40 of Circular 16/2025/TT-BXD).
h2
6. What to read in a detailed plan
p
Zoning management regulations under a detailed plan are stated for each land plot (Clause 3, Article 23 of Decree 178/2025/ND-CP). Homeowners should note down:
ol
The function of the plot (residential land, green space, transport land, etc.).
The land use indicators and construction elevation of the plot.
Building height, floor level, ground-floor height, architectural form, fencing and materials.
The red line and building line; safety corridors of technical infrastructure works.
Whether the plot is subject to conservation, renovation or upgrading.
p
With this information, the architect can design correctly from the start and the permit application is less likely to be returned – see Procedure for a Detached House Construction Permit 2026.
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The Law on Urban and Rural Planning 47/2024/QH15 and Decree 178/2025/ND-CP are currently partially no longer in effect (they have been amended); this article has cross-checked the amendments in Law 144/2025/QH15. The Ministry of Construction's regulations on how zoning information is provided on request are not yet in our library; ask the ward or commune People's Committee where the land is located directly.
